evidence.quote: In summary, a variety of factors have been holding down interest rates and may continue to do so for some time.
Lower trend increases in productivity and slower labor force growth imply lower overall economic growth in the years ahead.
The limitation on monetary policy imposed by low trend interest rates could therefore lead to longer and deeper recessions when the economy is hit by negative shocks.
Fed interest rates are kept very low at the moment because of the need to maintain aggregate demand at levels that will support the attainment of our dual policy goals
the evidence so far does not suggest a heightened threat of financial instability in the post-financial-crisis United States stemming from ultralow interest rates.

parsed.rationale: The speech argues that structural forces have pushed the equilibrium rate down and that the Fed cannot simply raise rates, implying a persistently low policy path. It also emphasizes downside risks from the effective lower bound and plays down financial-stability concerns, giving a moderately dovish lean.
